msgs: Caught above treeline when the storm hit. Hair standing up, poles buzzing. Ran for the trees and didn't stop until I was well below the ridge.
Hail and lightning on the exposed part. Nowhere to hide up there, so I just kept moving, fast, down to the first trees.
Thunderstorms forecast for tomorrow afternoon and a pass above treeline. Alarm set for an alpine start.
Thunder right overhead on the high stretch, the gap between flash and boom down to a second. Crouched on my pad between strikes, then moved fast.
Afternoon storms again tomorrow. Up early, over the high stuff by noon: that's the rule up here.
Found a trail angel's water cache the map doesn't show. Green and full of bugs. Filtered two litres anyway.
Water at a trail angel's water cache. Not on any map. Thank you, whoever keeps it running.
A day hiker gave me an orange. Best orange of my life.
Older couple on a day hike gave me a peach and asked a million questions. Lovely.
Weekend backpackers gave away their extra food at the trailhead. Scored a whole sleeve of Oreos.
Somebody's abandoned Snickers in a ziplock on a trail sign, with a note: "for a thru-hiker". Me!
Dry camp, and not enough water for dinner. Ate cold tortillas and went to bed thirsty.
Section hiker heading the other way handed me a cold Gatorade from his pack. Who carries that?
